# English copy review

The app's health content and its disclaimer, in Turkish and English, for review
by a native English speaker.

**Generated from the source catalogues** - do not edit this file by hand. It is
rebuilt and checked by `src/__tests__/english-review-package.test.ts`, so an
edit here is overwritten and a change in the app shows up here as a failing
test. Send corrections as comments or as a marked-up copy; they will be applied
to the catalogues.

## What to check for

The English was written from the cited sources rather than translated out of the
Turkish, so this is not a check that the two match word for word. It is a check
that they make **the same claim with the same strength**. Two failure directions,
and the second is the dangerous one:

1. **A hedge that weakened.** The NHS and Cleveland Clinic pages hedge
   constantly - "may", "might", "can", "usually", "some people". A hedge is easy
   to lose when a sentence is rewritten to read better, and the result is the app
   stating as fact something its source would not. If an English sentence sounds
   more certain than its Turkish counterpart, say so.
2. **A claim that strengthened.** The same thing one step further: an English
   sentence that asserts something the Turkish only suggests, or that adds a
   detail the Turkish does not carry. Anything in the English with no counterpart
   in the Turkish is worth flagging even if it reads well.

Also worth flagging:

- **Mood and feeling labels that read as statements.** Every one should be a
  "may", "might", "can" or "possible". A label that tells somebody how they feel
  is wrong however accurate it is on average.
- **Instructions the sources do not give.** Only two entries are meant to
  instruct rather than describe - weeks 31 and 40, which say to contact a doctor
  or midwife. An instruction anywhere else is a mistake.
- **Numbers and measurements.** The figures must be identical in both languages;
  they are the sources' own. Only the decimal mark differs - Turkish writes
  "25,6 cm" and English "25.6 cm", which is convention and not a discrepancy.
  The lengths also change basis between weeks 19 and 21 because the NHS pages do
  (head-to-bottom, then head-to-toe, then head-to-heel); that is deliberate and
  is not an error.
- **Anything that reads like a diagnosis**, or like the app telling somebody what
  is normal. It should never do either.
- **Plain unnaturalness.** Turkish-shaped English, a word that is not wrong but
  is not what a British or American reader would say. Flag it; naturalness is
  half of why this review exists.

Citations are deliberately **not translated**. They are English-language health
bodies and their page titles are what somebody would search for, so a translated
name would make a claim harder to check - which is the one thing a citation is
for.

The emergency line is deliberately **not the same** in the two languages: the
Turkish says 112 and the English says "contact your local emergency services"
and names no number. A language is not a country. This is intentional and is not
a translation that drifted.


## 1. The disclaimer

The highest-stakes copy in the app. The wording is fixed on purpose: a
screen that cannot fit these sentences is a screen that needs changing, not
a reason to shorten them. Read these first and read them hardest.

### The onboarding screen, shown once before anything else

#### Title

**Turkish**

```text
Başlamadan önce
```

**English**

```text
Before you start
```

#### Introduction

**Turkish**

```text
Bu uygulama regl döngünü ve gebeliğini takip etmene yardımcı olur. Gösterdiği tarihler ve bilgiler, girdiğin kayıtlara dayanan tahminlerdir.
```

**English**

```text
This app helps you keep track of your cycle and your pregnancy. The dates and information it shows are estimates based on the records you enter.
```

### The three points

A list rather than a paragraph because these are the points somebody has to
be able to find again, and the middle one - that this is not contraception -
is the one a wall of text would swallow.

#### Point 1 - Not medical advice

**Turkish**

```text
Tıbbi tavsiye, teşhis veya tedavi yerine geçmez.
```

**English**

```text
It is not a substitute for medical advice, diagnosis or treatment.
```

#### Point 2 - Not contraception

**Turkish**

```text
Doğum kontrol yöntemi olarak ya da gebe kalmak için tek başına kullanılmamalıdır.
```

**English**

```text
It must not be used on its own as a method of contraception or to conceive.
```

#### Point 3 - Emergency

**Turkish**

```text
Sağlığınla ilgili bir endişen varsa bir sağlık profesyoneline danış. Acil bir durumda 112'yi ara.
```

**English**

```text
If you have any concern about your health, speak to a healthcare professional. In an emergency, contact your local emergency services.
```

### The long form, on the About screen

#### Paragraph 1

**Turkish**

```text
Regl & Gebelik Takvimi, girdiğin kayıtlara dayanarak döngü evreleri, doğurganlık penceresi, ovülasyon günü ve tahmini doğum tarihi gibi tahminler gösterir. Herkesin döngüsü farklıdır; bu tahminler kesin değildir.
```

**English**

```text
Regl & Gebelik Takvimi shows estimates - cycle phases, the fertile window, the day of ovulation and an estimated due date - based on the records you enter. Every cycle is different, and these estimates are not certainties.
```

#### Paragraph 2

**Turkish**

```text
Uygulamadaki içerikler genel bilgilendirme amaçlıdır. Tıbbi tavsiye, teşhis veya tedavi yerine geçmez.
```

**English**

```text
The content in this app is for general information. It is not a substitute for medical advice, diagnosis or treatment.
```

#### Paragraph 3

**Turkish**

```text
Uygulama bir doğum kontrol yöntemi değildir. Gebelikten korunmak ya da gebe kalmak için tek başına kullanılmamalıdır.
```

**English**

```text
This app is not a method of contraception. It must not be used on its own to avoid pregnancy or to conceive.
```

#### Paragraph 4

**Turkish**

```text
Gebelik süresince düzenli doktor kontrollerini aksatma. Sağlığınla ilgili bir endişen varsa bir sağlık profesyoneline danış. Acil bir durumda 112'yi ara.
```

**English**

```text
Keep up with your regular check-ups throughout a pregnancy. If you have any concern about your health, speak to a healthcare professional. In an emergency, contact your local emergency services.
```

### The footer under every piece of health content

One line, shown under the daily cycle note and under every pregnancy week.

**Turkish**

```text
Genel bilgilendirme amaçlıdır, tıbbi tavsiye değildir.
```

**English**

```text
For general information only. This is not medical advice.
```


## 2. The four cycle phases

Shown on the home screen with the disclaimer footer beneath it. One message
per phase, plus mood labels where the sources support them.

### 1. The menstrual phase

**Support message**

**Turkish**

```text
Bu günlerde hafif bir yürüyüş bazı kişilere iyi gelebilir. Nasıl hissettiğin kişiden kişiye değişir; kendine alan tanı.
```

**English**

```text
A gentle walk suits some people on these days. How you feel varies from person to person; give yourself room.
```

**Mood labels**

| Turkish | English |
| --- | --- |
| Kramplar olabilir | Cramps are possible |
| Harekete geçmek önceki haftalara göre kolaylaşabilir | Moving may feel easier than it did the week before |

Each of these should read as a possibility, not a statement.

**Sources**

- Office on Women's Health — Physical activity and your menstrual cycle  
  <https://womenshealth.gov/getting-active/physical-activity-menstrual-cycle>
- Office on Women's Health — Your menstrual cycle and your health  
  <https://womenshealth.gov/menstrual-cycle/your-menstrual-cycle-and-your-health>

### 2. The follicular phase

**Support message**

**Turkish**

```text
Enerjin yerindeyse keyif aldığın şeylere zaman ayırmak için uygun bir aralık olabilir. Herkeste böyle olmayabilir.
```

**English**

```text
If your energy is there, this may be a good stretch for the things you enjoy. It is not like this for everybody.
```

**Mood labels**

| Turkish | English |
| --- | --- |
| Enerji biraz daha yüksek olabilir | Energy may be a little higher |
| Hafıza daha açık olabilir | Memory may feel clearer |
| Ağrı eşiği daha yüksek olabilir | Pain may be easier to tolerate |

Each of these should read as a possibility, not a statement.

**Sources**

- Office on Women's Health — Your menstrual cycle and your health  
  <https://womenshealth.gov/menstrual-cycle/your-menstrual-cycle-and-your-health>
- Office on Women's Health — Physical activity and your menstrual cycle  
  <https://womenshealth.gov/getting-active/physical-activity-menstrual-cycle>

### 3. The ovulatory phase

**Support message**

**Turkish**

```text
Yumurtlama günlerinde ruh halinin nasıl olacağına dair kaynaklarda net bir bilgi yok. Kendini nasıl hissediyorsan o geçerli.
```

**English**

```text
The sources say nothing definite about how mood goes around ovulation. However you feel is what counts.
```

**Mood labels:** none, deliberately.

The cited pages say nothing about mood at ovulation. The popular "energetic, cheerful ovulation" label has nothing behind it in these sources, so the app says nothing rather than repeating it.

**Sources**

- Office on Women's Health — Your menstrual cycle and your health  
  <https://womenshealth.gov/menstrual-cycle/your-menstrual-cycle-and-your-health>
- Office on Women's Health — Physical activity and your menstrual cycle  
  <https://womenshealth.gov/getting-active/physical-activity-menstrual-cycle>

### 4. The luteal phase

**Support message**

**Turkish**

```text
Regl öncesi günlerde belirtiler herkeste aynı değildir, aydan aya da değişebilir. Hareket, uyku ve kendine nazik davranmak bazı kişilere iyi gelebilir.
```

**English**

```text
In the days before a period, symptoms are not the same for everybody and can differ from month to month. Moving, sleeping and being kind to yourself help some people.
```

**Mood labels**

| Turkish | English |
| --- | --- |
| Yorgunluk veya ağırlık hissi olabilir | Tiredness or heaviness is possible |
| Unutkanlık olabilir | Forgetfulness is possible |
| Ruh hali dalgalanmaları olabilir | Mood may swing |
| Tatlı ya da unlu yiyeceklere istek artabilir | Cravings for sweet or starchy food may rise |
| Uykuya dalmak zorlaşabilir | Falling asleep may get harder |

Each of these should read as a possibility, not a statement.

**Sources**

- NHS — Premenstrual syndrome (PMS)  
  <https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/pre-menstrual-syndrome/>
- Office on Women's Health — Your menstrual cycle and your health  
  <https://womenshealth.gov/menstrual-cycle/your-menstrual-cycle-and-your-health>
- Office on Women's Health — Physical activity and your menstrual cycle  
  <https://womenshealth.gov/getting-active/physical-activity-menstrual-cycle>


## 3. The forty pregnancy weeks

Shown one week at a time on the home screen in pregnancy mode, each with the
disclaimer footer beneath it. The NHS week-by-week guide is the primary
source from week 4 on; Cleveland Clinic is cited alongside as corroboration.
Where the two put a milestone in different weeks, the week here is the NHS
one.

**Weeks 31 and 40 are the only two entries meant to instruct** - they say to
contact a doctor or midwife. Everywhere else the content describes and does
not advise.

### Week 1

**Development summary**

**Turkish**

```text
Gebelik yaşı, son regl döneminin ilk gününden itibaren sayılır. Bu nedenle ilk haftada henüz döllenme gerçekleşmemiştir; vücut olası bir gebeliğe hazırlanmaya başlar.
```

**English**

```text
Gestational age is counted from the first day of your last period. So in the first week fertilisation has not happened yet; the body begins preparing for a possible pregnancy.
```

**Size:** none for this week, deliberately. Gestational age is counted
from the last menstrual period, so there is nothing yet whose size is
worth stating.

**What is developing**

| Turkish | English |
| --- | --- |
| Gebelik yaşı son regl döneminin ilk gününden sayılır | Gestational age is counted from the first day of the last period |
| Hormon düzeyleri kademeli olarak yükselir | Hormone levels rise gradually |
| Rahim olası bir gebeliğe hazırlanır | The womb prepares for a possible pregnancy |

**Sources**

- Cleveland Clinic — Fetal Development: Week-by-Week Stages of Pregnancy  
  <https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/articles/7247-fetal-development-stages-of-growth>


**English**

```text
The body goes on preparing. Towards the middle of the cycle a ripened follicle opens and releases an egg from the ovary; this is ovulation.
```

**Development summary**

**Turkish**

**English**

## 4. The strings that make a claim without a citation

Sections 2 and 3 are written from medical sources and carry them. These are
not. They are the app's own sentences about somebody's body, written in
Turkish and then written again in English, and nothing outside the
repository they live in has ever read the English half.

### What to check for in this section

These fail differently from the health content, and the difference matters
more than the resemblance. A week note fails by sounding like advice. These
fail in three other ways:

1. **A limit that reads as a fact.** Most of 4e exists to stop the app
   claiming something: that a prediction has run out, that a count is
   arithmetic rather than a forecast, that a fertility figure is a guess.
   English can turn a refusal into an assertion without altering the meaning
   of a single word. "The expected day has passed" is a boundary; "Your
   period is late" would be a finding about a person, and the app does not
   know that. If a sentence written to withhold reads like a result, that is
   the failure, and it is the one most likely to be missed because the
   sentence will read perfectly well.
2. **A label that tells somebody how they are.** "Luteal", "Highest", "How
   you might feel". These appear as a value beside a date with no sentence
   around them to soften anything. Each has to be readable as an estimate
   drawn from an average cycle. One that reads as a measurement of this
   person in this month is wrong however right it is on average - and in
   English a single word carries more certainty than its Turkish counterpart
   more often than the reverse, because English has fewer ways to be
   tentative in one word.
3. **More said than was meant to be.** The six strings in 4a arrive on a
   locked phone. See below.

The two directions from section 1 - a hedge that weakened, a claim that
strengthened - apply here as well and are not repeated.

### Six of these are read by somebody who is not the user

Everything in 4a is delivered as a notification, which Android prints on the
lock screen whether the app would prefer it or not. The app asked not to,
with the option that exists for exactly that, and the platform discarded it -
so the only thing it controls is the wording, and that is what 4a is.

Read those six as if over a shoulder, on a phone lying on a table in a
shared room. The question is not whether the sentence is accurate. It is
what somebody who is not the user learns from it. The Turkish was written
against that test; the English has never been held to it by anyone.

The discreet pair exists for people who need less said: one wording for both
reminders, so that nothing in the words distinguishes a period reminder from
a pregnancy one. If the English discreet lines give away which reminder
arrived - by tone, by register, by a word the other would not use - that
defeats the setting, and it is the single most important thing in this
section.

What it does not hide, and does not claim to: the app's name and its icon
are on the notification. 4b's first entry is the sentence that admits that.
Check that it admits it plainly in English too.

### The mechanical check has already been run, and found nothing

Section 1's first check - a hedge that weakened - is the one a rule can
approximate, so it was tried: all 54 pairs in sections 2 and 3, Turkish
hedging matched against English hedging. **One hit, and it was wrong.** Week
24's Turkish "yaşayabilir" is the quoted technical term that the English
carries as the quoted "viable", and the English hedges in a way the pattern
could not see - "would have a chance of surviving".

So there is no rule-detectable hedge asymmetry anywhere in this document, and
the scan was not kept. A check that passes on everything and has never caught
anything is worse than no check, because the next person reads the green and
stops looking.

That is said here for two reasons: so nobody writes it again, and because it
locates what is left. What remains is the part no pattern reaches - whether a
sentence sounds natural, whether it sounds like advice, whether it sounds
more certain than the thing it describes. That is the whole of why a person
is being asked.

### What is not in this section, and why

A string is here if it **makes or withholds a claim about the person's body,
or about a prediction of it**. That admits "Luteal" and "The expected day has
passed"; it excludes "Takvim", "Bugün", "Kaydet" and the thousand or so other
interface strings, none of which say anything about anybody.

Six strings a looser reading would have admitted are deliberately out: row
labels that name a claim without making one, and the calendar legend's
period mark, which describes a record rather than a prediction. If the rule
has drawn that line in the wrong place, say so - that is more useful than a
section that grew because nobody wanted to argue about it.

47 pairs in all.

### 4a. What a reminder says

All six of these arrive on a locked phone. Read them as described above:
not whether the sentence is accurate, but what somebody who is not the
user learns from it.

### 4e. Where the app stops claiming

Most of these exist to withhold something. A limit that reads as a fact
is the failure to look for, and it is the one easiest to miss, because
the sentence will read perfectly well.

#### `supportDisclaimer`

**Turkish**

```text
Bu bilgiler geneldir; kişiden kişiye ve aydan aya değişebilir.
```

**English**

```text
This is general information; it varies from person to person and month to month.
```

**Turkish**

```text
Doğurganlık bilgileri tahminidir ve gebelikten korunma yöntemi olarak kullanılmamalıdır.
```

```text
Fertility information is an estimate and must not be used as a method of contraception.
```

## Returning this



Mark up anything that reads unnaturally, anything where the English is more

or less certain than the Turkish, and anything that sounds like advice or a

diagnosis. A sentence that is fine can be left alone - silence on an entry

is taken to mean it passed.
